## Blocking findings

### F1 — P1, S02: nested replacement deletes fields without recording them

`convex/lib/journal.ts:46`, `:51`, `:106`.

`diffFields` traverses only keys present in the supplied nested object, but `db.patch` replaces the
whole top-level object. For a foe whose `live` includes conditions, patching
`live: { stamina: 14, temporaryStamina: 0 }` removes `live.conditions` in storage while the journal
contains only `live.stamina: 15 → 14`. Undo cannot restore the missing conditions. A deletion-only
nested replacement is also liable to be skipped because no changes are detected.

Reproduced through `journalPatch`, followed by independent reads of the foe and command journal.
Diff the complete nested replacement, including omitted keys, or apply a deliberately merged object
whose actual stored change matches the journal. The existing `diffFields` test assumes the wrong
semantics for omitted nested fields and therefore misses this.

### F2 — P1, A01/S02 integration: command identity differs between receipts and dice/history

`convex/lib/commands.ts:29`, `convex/lib/dice.ts:104`, `convex/lib/journal.ts:171`.

Receipts deduplicate by authenticated user plus command ID, but dice and undo units use campaign plus
command ID. A player can copy the command ID of a Director's public roll and submit the same dice:
the app creates a second independently attributed event using the **same accepted roll**, without
advancing the random stream. Both user events then appear in one `commandJournal` undo unit.
Public history exposes these IDs, so this permits selecting a known roll, not merely an improbable
random ID collision. Different dice under that ID instead incorrectly refuse a legitimate second user.

Reproduced with two authenticated issuers, two persisted events, one persisted roll, and one combined
journal. Use one consistent authenticated command identity throughout execution, dice and history;
do not depend on client UUID uniqueness to enforce this boundary.

### F3 — P1, A01: a card can execute for a different actor than its stored binding

`convex/lib/interactions.ts:79`, `convex/lib/registry.ts:374`.

The continuation preserves the originally typed name, then rebinds that name during response.
`boundActor` is only used to compare an explicitly supplied response actor, not to select the actor
for ordinary headless responses. Open `@Thorn /table roll`, rename that hero, create another controlled
hero named Thorn, and respond: the card still stores the original actor ID while the resulting event
records the replacement actor ID. Renaming alone makes a valid existing card unanswerable.

Reproduced using persisted card and event reads. Store/resume the stable bound reference and recheck
current control of that same entity. The stored name remains the display label, not the identity.

### F4 — P1, A01: a closed-session card can resume in a later session

`convex/lib/interactions.ts:56`, `:79`; `convex/interactions.ts:120`.

Response checks status and campaign, but never checks the card's session against the current session.
Opening a roll card, closing its session, starting another session, and answering the old card succeeds.
It changes the old card to resolved and writes its consequence into the new session, linked to the old
session's event. This violates permanently read-only closed sessions and the specified card boundary.

Reproduced using the public session and response mutations, reading back both session IDs and status.
Reject/invalidate continuations outside their owning session; card closure needs the same lifecycle
check rather than permitting mutation of a historical card.

### F5 — P2, A01: closing a card is unlogged and absent from the registry

`convex/interactions.ts:141`, `:157`; `convex/lib/interactions.ts:113`;
`convex/lib/registry.ts:433`.

The close mutation updates the interaction and receipt without an attributed event. There is no
registered closure command, so the declared single table-operation path is incomplete. Reproduced:
closing a pending card changes its status, leaves event count unchanged, and no close operation appears
in `commands.list`. Implement closure through an attributed registered operation with headless parity.

### F6 — P1, A03: hidden Malice and difficulty leak through public history

`convex/lib/tableOperations.ts:497`, `:259`; `convex/events.ts:72`, `:74`.

With Show Malice off, `/adjust malice value=47` still gives observers the literal description
`0 → 47`, `payload.data.after: 47`, and the submitted value in the envelope. The roster's null Malice
projection does not protect the pool. Likewise `/test roll ... difficulty=hard` writes `hard` into
both description and payload, and all members receive it. The required default-off Show test difficulty
setting is absent; the owning spec also requires it to affect historical displayed tests.

Both leaks reproduced through observer `events.list` reads. Apply audience projection to descriptions,
structured result data and recorded envelopes, preserving public dice/workings/outcomes. Implement the
difficulty setting rather than hiding only one rendered label.

### F7 — P1, A03: the other foe query bypasses health-display privacy

`convex/foes.ts:89`.

`table.roster` correctly returns only `{ mode: 'winded', winded: false }` for a foe at 12/15 under
Winded mode, but any observing member can call `foes.list` and obtain `healthFraction: 0.8` for the same
foe. This older shared read remains callable and used by the application. Reproduced through both
queries. Make all current foe projections obey the same selected health mode.

### F8 — P1, A03: peer roster exposes all hero live resources

`convex/table.ts:87`; `web/table/index.tsx:384`.

Every member receives the full `liveState` of every attached hero, including Heroic Resource, XP,
Surges and Victories. The party view permits peer Stamina/Recoveries, with additional permissions kept
separate. The slice note claiming that visibility was not narrowed contradicts that owning section.
Reproduced by setting Thorn's Heroic Resource to 7 and reading it as an observer.

Project own/authorized-sheet data separately from limited peer data and ensure the corresponding UI
uses that projection. This finding concerns current live resources, not an invented blanket ban on
historical public action text.

### F9 — P2, A03: exposed foe removal bypasses the command registry

`web/table/index.tsx:252`; `convex/lib/registry.ts:433`.

The running-table Remove button calls `api.foes.remove` directly, which is not registered/discoverable
in `commands.list`. The action is a real shared mutation, but cannot be invoked through the promised
`pnpm app command` path or palette. Register the exposed foe operation and route the button through it.
The same integration work should cover the existing add flow; no dormant hide/reveal feature is requested.

### F10 — P2, A03: Recovery's source expander contains no verbatim source text

`convex/lib/tableOperations.ts:326`; `web/table/index.tsx:483`, `:491`.

The Recovery event contains only a source ID and an implementation note. `EventSource` renders source
text only when `source.text` already exists and does not resolve the ID. Consequently its “Source”
expansion cannot show the used action's required complete verbatim text. Supply the pinned content text
and provenance through the shared event/read path. This is incomplete source disclosure, not an error
in the verified healing arithmetic.

## Independent A03 rules verification

Only the pinned local Compendium was used. Read `rule/dice/power-roll.md`, `edge.md`, `bane.md`,
`bonuses-and-penalties.md`, `natural-roll.md`, `natural-19-20.md`, `tier-outcome.md`,
`rule/test/test.md`, `rule/test/test-difficulty.md`, `chapter/tests.md` (skills and examples),
`chapter/the-basics.md` (Recovery context), `rule/health/recoveries.md`,
`feature/common/maneuvers/catch-breath.md`, and `rule/general/always-round-down.md`.

Source-derived expectations, independently compared with code and tests:

- Tests roll 2d10 plus the supplied characteristic, agreed skill +2 and the net edge/bane modifier.
  Capping each count at two before cancellation is correct: three edges plus one bane leaves one edge.
- Totals 11/12/16/17 yield tiers 1/2/2/3. Double edge/bane shifts the tier once with 1–3 bounds,
  not an additional numeric ±2. The Easy/Medium/Hard outcome tables match the local source.
- Natural 19/20 gives the recorded critical test success/reward; double-bane conflict keeps the R04
  provisional tier-3 interpretation and adds `Q-R-1`. No critical attack extra action is invented.
- No difficulty means no computed outcome label. The characteristic is explicitly a supplied fact,
  not falsely claimed to come from a completed hero evaluator. Additional source-specific bonuses,
  automatic outcomes and narrative consequences are not certified by this bounded slice.
- Recovery value is floor(maximum/3): maxima 30/31/32/33 produce 10/10/10/11. One Recovery is deducted;
  maximum 30 and Stamina 22 heals 8 to 30, Stamina 19 heals 10 to 29, and full health spends one for
  zero healing. The cap follows R04's provisional `Q-R-3`, not an asserted unambiguous source rule.
  The two resource changes persist in one event's journal; temporary Stamina is not refilled.

The arithmetic pass does not resolve the existing Q-R questions, certify combat maneuver economy,
introduce dying automation, or approve F6/F10's disclosure behavior.

## Tests run and limitations

Ran:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run --project app tests/app/operations-audit.test.ts tests/app/journal.test.ts tests/app/dice.test.ts tests/app/registry.test.ts tests/app/interactions.test.ts tests/app/parse.test.ts tests/app/table.test.ts tests/app/engine-adapter.test.ts
8 files, 133 tests passed (125 existing + 8 audit probes).

pnpm exec vitest run --project app tests/app/operations-audit.test.ts
1 file, 9 tests passed (added the independent foes.list audience probe).
```

Audit probes assert the observed defects, not desired behavior. They were removed from normal discovery
and retained in `docs/build/audits/fixtures/operations-audit.test.ts.txt`. To rerun without adding them
to acceptance coverage:

```sh
cp docs/build/audits/fixtures/operations-audit.test.ts.txt tests/app/operations-audit.test.ts
pnpm exec vitest run --project app tests/app/operations-audit.test.ts
rm tests/app/operations-audit.test.ts
```

The `.txt` artifact is intentionally excluded from test discovery and typechecking. Its assertions
prove observations of defects; passing does not mean those behaviors are correct. No original test or
implementation file was changed.

The existing suites genuinely query persisted state/history rather than trusting mutation summaries.
Their gaps are scenario coverage: nested deletion, cross-user command IDs, closed-session cards, stable
actor binding, and alternate audience reads. Passing those suites alone did not establish correctness.
No full `pnpm check`, live deployment, real CLI invocation, browser execution, performance soak or live
network concurrency was performed by this subreview. Those claims require the parent's separate evidence.
